erikrose opened PR #15082 from erikrose:mmap-make-inaccessible to bytecodealliance:main:

Factor out what was getting to be a lot of repetition while I'm at it.

This is going to support the timing wheel in MMU interruption, getting a lot of unsafe code out of the wheel as compared to a lot of naked mprotect()s in its original implementation.

erikrose edited PR #15082:

Factor out what was getting to be a lot of repetition while I'm at it.

This is going to support the timing wheel in MMU interruption, getting a lot of unsafe code out of the wheel. (Its original implementation had a lot of naked mprotect()s.)

erikrose edited PR #15082:

Factor out what was getting to be a lot of repetition while I'm at it.

This is going to support the timing wheel in MMU interruption, allowing it to avoid calling a lot of naked mprotect()s on its own.

erikrose edited PR #15082:

I recently noticed we already have this mmap abstraction layer, so I might as well use it in the timing wheel in MMU interruption. It would bear fruit if we ever add more platform support. The overhead is negligible: there's only 1 extra syscall (vs. the raw mprotects I was using), and that's on page allocation, which is done only during warmup.

Factor out what was getting to be a lot of repetition as well.

erikrose edited PR #15082:

I recently noticed we already have this mmap abstraction layer, so I might as well use it in the timing wheel in MMU interruption. It would bear fruit if we ever add more platform support. It bears fruit now in reducing the number of conditional compilations referencing cfg(has_mmu_interruption). The overhead is negligible: there's only 1 extra syscall (vs. the raw mprotects I was using), and that's on page allocation, which is done only during warmup.

Factor out what was getting to be a lot of repetition as well.
